gateway: isolated temporary home, approval=reads; a freshly seeded gateway for the stub screenshots, one for the live ones and one for the walkthrough
data: fictional, seeded through the app's HTTP API (capture/scenes.json)

agent_backend.live_model: the operator's own installed, signed-in kiro-cli over ACP with model "auto"; the replies on screen are that model's and vary from run to run
agent_backend.stub: Kiro Crew's offline stub ACP backend (capture/stub_backend.py) for every other scene; no chat reply is shown from it
agent_backend.credit_reading: the browser answers the top bar's credit readout (/api/sessions/usage) with "no reading", so no account balance or email can be shown

note: The isolated gateway served this repository's own copy of the app: capture.py's setup installed it from a clean clone of the commit named in app_commit (POST /api/apps/install), trusted it and enabled it, and every picture shows its committed bundle (ui/dist/index.mjs) and its backend (backend/server.py), which the gateway spawned. Kiro Crew still ships a built-in design-tweak and refuses a second install under the same name, so the Kiro Crew tree the capture ran on is the App Kit level-1 commit with only the built-in copy removed (src/kiro_crew/apps/builtins/design_tweak); kirocrew_tree_dirty records that.
data_notes: The previewed web project is a made-up bakery site (Sunfield Bakery, sunfield-bakery.example) that capture/demo_site.py writes from scratch under the system temp directory before each pass ('prepare'); Design Tweak has no API that writes a project, because the project is the user's own code.

The folder was registered, selected and given its first two comments through the app's own API (POST /projects, /projects/select, /submit); every other comment was made in the pictures by right-clicking the preview.
Comments carry the time the backend received them, so their ages read as seconds or minutes before the picture.

The edits shown as done were made by a live model through the operator's own kiro-cli, in the project's own chat session, after the session was trusted on screen; its wording and the exact CSS it wrote differ from run to run.
